blocks.title: Beaches
blocks.body: Crete is a magical island filled with myth and legend, a place to relax the ideal choice for all the family.
paragraphs: Crete is a magical island filled with myth and legend, a place to relax the ideal choice for all the family.
The closest beaches to the villa that we suggest you to visit are:
- Villas' private beach which is only 50m distance.

- Rethymno beach which is just 8 km away from the villa. Rethymno beach is located 500m east of the city centre and it is a beach with golden sand and crystal clear shallow water, very well organized and close to all amenities of the city. It offers numerous beach bars, restaurants and cafes that offer umbrellas with sun beds, showers and changing rooms. Additionally on Rethymno�s beach you may find water sports facilities. Furthermore, there is a boardwalk which is ideal for afternoon walks by the sea, or simply shopping or dining.

- Ammoudaki beach: The turquoise waters and spectacular white coarse sand, make this small beach popular destination for nudists. Moreover, on the beach there is a small canteen, which also provides umbrellas and sun beds. At the west side of the beach, you can swim till a marine cave, where the sun rays make the color of the water vivid blue. The seabed is sandy and you can walk there. At the other end, there is an under water hole that connects Ammoudaki with Klisidi. So you can get from one beach to another only with a dive. To reach the beaches of Ammoudi on foot, you can walk east of Damnoni, till you meet Ammoudaki.

- Damnoni beach : Here you will find all the services of a well organized beach such as umbrellas, snack bars, showers, changing rooms, water sports, scuba diving centre, great hotels, restaurants, one horse riding centre etc. The west end of the beach, the most organized part, has a small river with water almost all year round. The east end of the beach is quieter and is linked with the adjacent beaches of Ammoudakii via a short dirt road. Moreover, beyond the west end of the beach there are several small coves with sand and rocks, where you can get isolated. These are located just next to the small harbor of the area.

The distance to the South coast from the villa is about 40 minutes by car and all the above beaches are located near to Plakias village where you can find shops and many taverns.

Moreover, on the beach there is a small canteen, which also provides umbrellas and sun beds. At the west side of the beach, you can swim till a marine cave, where the sun rays make the color of the water vivid blue. The seabed is sandy and you can walk there. Furthermore, On the South coast of the island you can also discover some of Crete's most amazing natural beaches such as “Schinaria”, “Triopetra”, “Agios Pavlos” and "Preveli". The distance to the South coast from the villa is about 40 minutes by car and all the above beaches are located near to Plakias village where you can find shops and many taverns.

todos: RESOLVED since the first pass: the previous note claiming 'the location section states NO distances and NO named nearby attractions, so nearby is an empty array' was WRONG. It was true only of the crawled static HTML. Modal 1898 is baked into the page bundle and injected by Angular; /en/page/modal/article/1898 returns 404 on the live host. The full 7-paragraph text and 11 images are now folded in from content/modals.json and 'nearby' holds 11 named places.

Encoding: the live source of modal 1898 contains genuine U+FFFD replacement characters (irrecoverable mojibake upstream, not a decoding error on our side). 'paragraphs' preserves them verbatim; 'paragraphsNormalized' supplies the obvious intended characters - an apostrophe in "Rethymno's" and "Crete's", and curly double quotes around “Schinaria”, “Triopetra” and “Agios Pavlos”. The fourth beach name is quoted with straight ASCII quotes in the source ("Preveli") and is left that way in both variants - the inconsistency is in the source.

Source typo (left as-is): 'the adjacent beaches of Ammoudakii' in paragraph 6 has a doubled final 'i'; the same beach is spelled 'Ammoudaki' everywhere else and 'the beaches of Ammoudi' in paragraph 5. Three spellings for one place.
Source typo (left as-is): 'Damnoni beach :' has a space before the colon, and 'Furthermore, On the South coast' capitalises 'On' mid-sentence.

blocks[0].body is the single teaser paragraph rendered on the homepage (identical to paragraphs[0]); the remaining six paragraphs are visible only inside the modal. The teaser paragraph is marked 'hidden-xs' in the source, i.e. it is not shown on mobile at all.

blocks[0].image is the section's parallax background, taken from the section's data-pages-bg-image attribute (a .webp twin exists at .../33dfaa1f26817d5a1b09235e185cc753.webp). It is not an tag and does not appear in content/assets/en__index-1.imgs.txt. It is also images[0] of the modal gallery.

blocks[0].href is null: the block's 'Read more...' control is a button, not a link (data-ng-click="loadArticlesModal('en',1898);" data-target="#article_modal1898"). The Location section therefore has no linkable page. A real destination URL is needed.

The 11 modal images have no captions or alt text identifying which beach each one shows, so no image can be matched to a named place. Visual review or client input required before the redesign can pair photos with beaches.

The distances are marketing copy, not measured figures: '8 km' to Rethymno beach, '50m' to the private beach and 'about 40 minutes by car' to the South coast are the only quantities stated anywhere. Ammoudaki, Damnoni, Klisidi, Schinaria, Triopetra, Agios Pavlos, Preveli and Plakias have no stated distance and their 'distance' is null - do not estimate them.

The Google Maps marker cluster array in the page script is empty (var clusters = [];), so none of these 11 places is plotted; the map has a single marker for the villas. The page renders no map container at all (id="lodge-map" is styled in CSS but never output; the after_map SECTION is empty), so the map is not actually displayed on the homepage.
The h3/h4/h5 slots in the location section contain only the placeholder character 'n' (CMS chrome) and are ignored.

address.lines are copied verbatim from the contact section of the index page, including the trailing comma on 'Rethymno,'. 'Thalasses Villas' is the block-title above the <address> element, included as the first line.

address.region is set to 'Rethymno' from the page's schema.org Organization JSON-LD ("addressLocality": "Rethymno"); the page never states a Greek administrative region or the word 'Crete' in this address block. The JSON-LD calls 'Pigianos Kampos area' the "streetAddress" - no actual street name or number is given for the villas.

Source inconsistency (left as-is): the map info-window writes the place name as 'Pigianos kampos ' (lowercase 'k', trailing space) while the contact block writes 'Pigianos Kampos area'. The info-window also carries its own image: https://s3-eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/loggia-cdn/lodgeContent/01e5107612a2f4f472c6b9d19d5025b9.jpg and heading 'Pigianos Kampos'.
coordinates and mapUrl come from the page's Google Maps script/marker info-window (marker id 2291, zoom 11), not from any visible text. They are unchanged from the first pass.

A different address appears elsewhere on the page, inside the Terms & Conditions boilerplate ('Trantallidou 13-15 Rethymno, 74100 Crete' - the registered company office). It was NOT used here because it is not the villas' location.
No airport, port or town-centre distance is stated anywhere on the site. Rethymno is the only settlement given a distance, and only as a beach.

The section eyebrow/heading pair is 'Location' (h6 block-title) / 'Beaches' (h2). The section is titled after beaches but is the site's only Location content, so the redesign will need a decision: is this a Location section or a Beaches section?
Owner-confirmed distances added (cafes 650 m through Chania port 61.2 km). These are distinct from the beach descriptions recovered from modal 1898, which remain in 'nearby'.
